nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Climate-smart crop selection_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Which diploid ancestor of wheat is examined for its genome-wide environmental scans (GWES) in this study?
nodes.answer: The diploid ancestor examined is Aegilops tauschii (Ae. tauschii).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Climate-smart crop selection_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What has been the focus of kelp breeders in terms of temperature tolerance?
nodes.answer: They have been developing high temperature tolerant varieties to extend growing time and increase yield.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Climate-smart crop selection_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What are some recommendations for wine-growing regions like South Moravia and the Bermuda Region to adapt to climate change?
nodes.answer: In South Moravia and the Bermuda Region, the scientists suggest growing heat-loving varieties like Mourned or Grenade to replace grape varieties like Pinot Noir, Cabernet Sauvignon, and Merlot that may not thrive in the new climatic conditions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Climate-smart crop selection_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What makes the prioritization of genebank germplasm for breeding climate-adapted wheat varieties challenging?
nodes.answer: The prioritization is challenging due to the polygenic nature of adaptation to varied environments.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Climate-smart crop selection_qna_004
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How does the second approach enhance the selection of wild relative accessions?
nodes.answer: It is based on environmental parameters at the site of accession origin.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Sustainable agriculture practices|Climate-smart crop selection_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Which two wild ancestors of wheat are mentioned as important for broadening the climate adaptive potential of modern wheat?
nodes.answer: Aegilops tauschii and Triticum turgidum ssp. dicoccodies (wild emmer) are mentioned as important wild ancestors.
